Separate Gitaly gold-policy backup and PostgreSQL 30-day backup storage from GitLab application backups in the 11 buckets.
Removed implicit load-balancer free-tier deductions; all extended costs use gross quantity x rate and decimal half-up cent rounding.

calculation_notes: A quantity of zero on an UNSET line means no usage cost has been included; it is not a zero-usage assertion. The complete monthly estimate remains null until usage inputs are supplied.
Monthly SKU amounts are not multiplied by 744; hourly SKUs are. Request quantity is in units of 10,000 requests.
Database storage is shared across its three nodes; do not multiply storage blindly by replica count. Storage is dynamically metered.

The old export used 30 VPUs per database storage GiB for the 75K tier. Oracle billing documents confirm VPU charging, but the exact managed-service mapping was not verified here; supply billable VPU-GB usage or confirm with the estimator before finalizing.

Gitaly snapshot and PostgreSQL backup storage use standard Object Storage rates. Application backups already belong in the application bucket total; do not count them again as managed database or volume backups.
Object versions have no lifecycle expiry configured. Storage can grow even when current live object size is unchanged.
Load balancer billed bandwidth can rise to the configured 1000 Mbps maximum per LB. Full-month gross minimum is 31.69 USD; full-month 2x1000 Mbps is 165.61 USD.
Free allowances are shared/eligibility-dependent. The previous LB cost implicitly deducted one instance and 10 Mbps; this review reports gross cost to avoid assuming those credits are available.
Boot and ephemeral scratch performance is budgeted at the default Balanced 10 VPUs/GiB. Review if the CSI storage class or boot performance is changed.
19 user-managed/OKE VMs are counted, plus 6 managed PostgreSQL nodes. Additional Kubernetes pods on existing workers are not separately billed compute.
Changing runner_count, mode, shapes, repository size, replicas, storage class, backup scratch or LB limits requires updating this estimate.
